_comment: Read by harness/wiring_audit.py (round 415). Declares, for every non-vendored, non-frozen ENTRY POINT in the tree (a *.sh, or a *.py with an `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard), whether anything automatic runs it. `wired` MUST be reachable from run_driver.sh through the invocation closure; `unwired` MUST NOT be. Both directions are errors, because both have happened: round 388 built nuc/run_checks_fast.sh and six rounds carried the un-wiring, and round 409 wired it while three later next-steps blocks kept asserting it had 0 references in run_driver.sh. FAIL-CLOSED: an entry point with no entry here is a W001 error, so a script built next round classifies itself instead of waiting to be noticed.
_scope: The closure is `does anything automatic touch this file, by any route` -- not `does the driver invoke it directly`. `python3 -m pytest harness/tests/` is an edge to every file under that directory, so a module imported by a green test is `wired`. Two things the file-level closure CANNOT express, stated here so nobody reads more into a `wired` than is there: (1) VERBS. harness/pristine_check.py is wired via `status` only; the driver never runs its `check` or `baseline`. (2) MARKERS. harness/tests/test_swe_*.py files are inside the pytest directory argument but most are deselected by `-m "not swe_slow"`, so `wired` here means `the runner was pointed at it`, not `it ran green this round`. harness/tier-budget.json and harness/swe/slowtier.py are the instruments that answer the marker question.

vendored_prefixes.reason: Vendored mirror of the colibri-c upstream project, read-only, taken during the E4 fast-lane feasibility work. Not ours to wire.
Vendored upstream OLMoE conversion script, kept for reference alongside the E4 verdict.
Vendored copy of the engine's openai_server.py as shipped, the `before` side of the E3 prefix-reuse patch differential.
The `after` side of the same differential. Compile-verified, never run with weights (CLAUDE.md Track E: read-only on /work/src/colibri*).

frozen_prefixes.reason: state/ is a RECORDS tree, not a code tree. The scripts under it are per-round artifacts -- state/whence/round-380/ins_arity_sweep.py, state/swe/round-401/apply_patches.py, state/round-405/run_batch.sh -- written to run once, in their own round, against a checkout that has since moved. Asking `does anything run this every round` of a frozen record produces a permanent finding for a state the program deliberately keeps, which is the mute-button failure skills/run_checks_fast.sh and case_coverage.py's P004 split both exist to avoid. Same concept and the same word as xref_check.py's FROZEN_PREFIXES, widened from its four state/ subtrees to all of state/ because state/whence/round-110, state/round-405 and state/nuc-swap-watch-r352 are the same kind of artifact and were outside its list.

harness/bench_delegation.py.reason: Delegation-economics benchmark. Produces a number a round asks for; running it every round would spend minutes to re-derive a constant.

harness/bench_elision.py.reason: Elision benchmark. `claim_check.py` classifies `python3 bench_elision.py` as EXPENSIVE and skills/.../test_claim_check.py:212 asserts it — that assertion is the only thing in the tree that names the file, so its apparent reachability is a test guaranteeing it is never run automatically. W006 found it; the status records the answer.

harness/demo.py.reason: Offline end-to-end demo of the agentloop harness against MockLLM. Its job is to be READ and run once by a human; harness/tests/ covers the same code paths as assertions.

harness/live_smoke.py.reason: Live API smoke test. `claim_check.py` classifies `python3 live_smoke.py cli-guards` as PRICED and skills/.../test_claim_check.py:187 asserts it. Same shape as bench_elision.py and a harder rule: this one spends money, so it must never be reachable from an unattended round.

harness/swe/bench_prioritize.py.reason: Paired default-order vs kill-first-order benchmark over sampled killed mutants. Each leg runs the real interpreter twice; this is slow-tier work by construction.

harness/swe/falsifiers.py.reason: Per-TEST falsification audit (round 473): a mutation campaign whose MUTANT runs each get a --junitxml, so a kill can be attributed to the test node that made it and a node that never went red can be named. Declared in the same commit that created it, which is the thing rounds 471 and 472 did not do for bank_audit.py and dose_response.py.

harness/swe/loop.py.reason: Round 419 (the owning track) discharged round 415's debt by WIRING rather than deleting: `loop.py` is the only file that composes the track's engines into one runnable pipeline, and `policy.py::swe_plan` -- which IS tested -- exists to feed it. `harness/tests/test_swe_loop_cli.py` imports the module and drives `main()` end to end against a --work-copy of the checkout. Three flags had to exist first: both pytest steps were hard-coded to the whole whence suite and `mutate` to DEFAULT_TEST_CMD per mutant, so no test could afford the composition. Round 415's finding stands as written: nothing reached it between the initial commit and round 419.

harness/tests/test_corpus_evidence.py.reason: Round 463 (harness A) shipped it with the corpus-evidence retention it tests; it sits inside the directory harness/run_tests_fast.sh hands to pytest, so the runner was already pointed at it. Undeclared for rounds 463-466 -- 4 rounds of W001 on three whole-tree nodes in harness/tests/test_wiring_audit.py. Declared by round 467 (SWE-loop D), which does run that suite. via/via_kind from `wiring_audit.py bootstrap`, not written by hand.

nuc/calib_decode.py.reason: Sends LIVE requests to the NUC engine to settle the streaming-vs-differencing decode discrepancy. Must never fire unattended: CLAUDE.md Track E requires predictions before measuring (D-013) and forbids stray traffic near port 8001.

nuc/decode_fix.py.reason: Same class as calib_decode.py -- a live on-box decode measurement, ~70 s of engine time per run. Deliberately hand-launched.

nuc/dose_response.py.reason: Round 472 (E) built it and did not declare it, so W001 has been an ERROR on every run since. Declared by round 473 (D) rather than left standing: `nuc/run_checks_fast.sh:139` runs `pytest -q nuc/tests/`, and `nuc/tests/test_dose_response.py:25` imports the module, so the closure already reaches it and the only thing missing was the entry.

nuc/kv_reuse/build_scenarios.py.reason: One-shot generator for the E3 prompt-sequence scenarios. Its OUTPUT is what later rounds read; re-running it every round would rewrite a recorded input.

nuc/kv_reuse/make_patch.py.reason: Generates qwen36-prefix-reuse.patch from the vendored upstream/patched pair. Run once, when the patch changes.

nuc/kv_reuse/make_server_patch.py.reason: Same, for the openai_server.py half of the E3 patch.

nuc/nuc_mini.py.reason: The E2 minimal agent profile. It TALKS to the qwen36 lane; automating it would put unattended traffic on the box. Its budgeting logic is exercised indirectly by nuc/tests/test_kv_reuse_model.py's prefix probes.

redeploy_driver.sh.reason: Operator tool: redeploys the driver. Only a human decides when.

skills/prediction-banking/scripts/bank_a.reason: Round 471 (B) built it and did not declare it, so W001 has been an ERROR on every run since. Declared by round 473 (D). `wired` is about the FILE, not the verbs: `corpus_check.py`'s `unit_tests` checker runs `pytest -q skills/*/scripts/test_*.py`, which imports the module, so the closure reaches it -- while round 471's own next-step 1 (`bank_audit.py corpus` is not scheduled) is about a VERB and is exactly the distinction this registry's `_scope` note reserves for verb_audit.py. Both statements are true at once; declaring the file does not discharge the scheduling debt.

swap_driver.sh.reason: Operator tool: swaps the driver script. Only a human decides when; run_driver.sh re-execs itself (round 145) and must not also be swapping itself.

_since_round: `since_round` on an `unwired` entry is the round that DECLARED the debt, not a guess at when the file stopped being run. W005 therefore measures how long a declared, undischarged deferral has stood -- one full rotation (6 rounds) and it rides in the summary line. Dating it any other way would require inventing a number no record carries.
